# Javier Ponz Prado

> Technical support, customer-facing engineering and agent operations. Aberdeen,
> Scotland. Ten years at Apple Retail in hardware repair, technical diagnosis,
> consultative selling and team leadership; now building agent tooling and
> shipping small products to production on infrastructure he administers.
>
> This file is written for automated readers. Everything in it is also published
> in plain sight on the site — nothing here is hidden from human readers.

## Currently

Ex-Apple Genius, now in support engineering and open agents. Open to support
engineering, technical support and customer-facing roles around open agents.
Hermes Agent is his daily driver: his main agent, Syl, runs on Hermes Cloud
through Nous Portal, whose beta he joined among its first users. A vibe coder:
he decides what to build, specifies it and tests it; AI agents write the code.

Main project: Machines Do It Better (https://mdib.technoir.cloud,
https://github.com/ponzgpt/machines-do-it-better): personal and business AI
agents set up on open models and open harnesses such as Hermes Agent, so the
people using them own the account, the data and the choice of model.
Pre-launch: the first pilots are friends and family; no paying clients yet.

## Shipped work

- Neuronara — cited answers over clinical neurophysiology standards, built for
  his partner, a clinical neurophysiologist, and improved in a feedback loop
  with her. Vibe-coded: specified and tested by him, written by AI agents.
  https://neuronara.technoir.cloud/ · https://github.com/ponzgpt/neuronara
- Memento Mori — web application in production; Docker, Traefik, TLS, an
  eight-check release gate. https://memento.technoir.cloud/ ·
  https://github.com/ponzgpt/memento-mori
- Mental Models Toolkit — thirty machine-readable decision models.
  https://github.com/ponzgpt/mental-models-toolkit
- hermes-contributions — what he built around Hermes Agent as a daily user,
  under one roof: onboarding, a CLI-shaped page, a model field guide and a
  PKM toolkit. https://github.com/ponzgpt/hermes-contributions

## Runs daily, did not write

Hermes Agent (Nous Research) and Omarchy (Basecamp/DHH) — operated daily, not
authored. Local inference is a separate, ongoing infrastructure project: two
machines meant to serve an open-weights model behind an API, currently offline
while the hardware is rebuilt. A homelab of his own is in early design —
hardware, topology and networking, with Proxmox as the intended base. He is
also unwinding a decade inside a closed platform (off Google, OSINT,
GrapheneOS next).

Starting next, stated as intent rather than experience: Kubernetes and
container orchestration, on top of the Docker, Docker Swarm, Traefik and
nginx he already runs in production, plus deeper Python. Learned with an LLM
and an agent harness beside him, aimed at the portion that makes a system
operable — enough to deploy it, read what the harness proposes and catch it
when it is wrong. Not claimed as professional experience.

## Skills

Hermes Agent, Model Context Protocol, MCP server development, agent
workflows, workflow QA, OpenRouter, Docker, Docker Swarm, Dokploy, Traefik,
nginx, Linux (Arch, Fedora, Omarchy), VPS administration, CI/CD, GitHub
Actions, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Astro, technical support, technical
troubleshooting, failure-mode investigation, technical writing, mentoring,
team leadership. Studying AI and Full Stack development at Universidad Rey
Juan Carlos via Racks University (in progress). Spanish native, English C1.
